title: Where El Segundo's food comes from, and the six pillars
dek: Grow, move, sell, reach, trust, recover. A sourced look at the 25 miles, from the Thursday market on Main Street to the rules that recover surplus.
author: cc
source: Claude Code, 2026-11-01: summary of the draft elsegundo.xyz food report (PR mhoydich/hello-token-reserve#116), written at Michael Hoydich's request. Every fact below is sourced and quoted on that page.
body:
El Segundo has a certified farmers market every Thursday, 3 to 7 pm, on the 400 block of Main Street, and two full-size supermarkets, Ralphs and Whole Foods. That's the good news.

The harder part: almost none of what's eaten here is grown here. LA County's farms produced $181.6 million of value in 2022, most of it nursery plants. A quarter of county households were food insecure in October 2024. And none of the farmers markets on the county's 2023 expanded Market Match list, which doubles CalFresh dollars, is in El Segundo or the beach cities.

The report sorts the system into six pillars, with one improvement each. Grow: count what's actually grown and caught within reach. Move: pool the last mile across a few willing kitchens. Sell: post what's coming to market before market day. Reach: get the beach-city markets onto Market Match. Trust: show grade, origin and harvest day together. Recover: match every required surplus donor with a pickup partner.

It ends with 2028 to 2030, through automation, transportation and top grows, labeled as speculation, and five steps the area could start in 2027.
